text.arabic_uthmani: أَفَمَن زُيِّنَ لَهُۥ سُوٓءُ عَمَلِهِۦ فَرَءَاهُ حَسَنًۭا ۖ فَإِنَّ ٱللَّهَ يُضِلُّ مَن يَشَآءُ وَيَهْدِى مَن يَشَآءُ ۖ فَلَا تَذْهَبْ نَفْسُكَ عَلَيْهِمْ حَسَرَٰتٍ ۚ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ عَلِيمٌۢ بِمَا يَصْنَعُونَ

words.gloss_range: interrogative-plus-fa opening that launches a diagnostic rhetorical test
words.prose: {{ar:أَفَ}} ({{tr:a-fa}}) opens with both interrogative pressure and a sequential hinge, so the beautified-evil case enters as a challenge rather than a neutral report. The omitted counterpart makes the reader supply the comparison: is such a person like one rightly oriented? Even the variant without the fa only sharpens how strongly the standard surface keeps the argumentative bridge visible.

topics.headline: rhetorical diagnostic opening
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the ayah begins by testing a moral case, not by calmly describing it.
topics.reason: The hamza and fa jointly license a rhetorical challenge linked to the prior discourse.

topics.headline: omitted comparison and fa hinge
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices both the missing comparison and the standard reading’s visible fa-bridge into the case.
topics.reason: The variant is useful as contrast, while the canonical local surface keeps the fa hinge and the ellipsis active.

words.gloss_range: human relative pronoun forming an open person-type under the question
words.prose: {{ar:مَن}} ({{tr:man}}) supplies the human head of the opening clause. It keeps the deluded figure general, so the ayah diagnoses a repeatable type: whoever has evil beautified for him and then judges it good. Under the opening question, the relative grammar becomes evaluative exposure rather than simple reference.

topics.headline: open human type under judgment
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the ayah holds up a type of person, not a named faction only.
topics.reason: The relative pronoun binds the following ṣila while the preceding interrogative colors the whole type as judged.

words.gloss_range: Form II passive beautification that changes appearance while leaving the bad object morally exposed
words.root_gloss_range: root range of adornment, attractive presentation, and beauty; here it is narrowed to deceptive moral beautification
words.prose: {{ar:زُيِّنَ}} ({{tr:zuyyina}}) is the ayah’s perceptual engine. Its Form II passive intensifies the beautifying overlay while leaving the beautifier offstage, so scrutiny falls on the altered appearance and the person who accepts it. Because {{ar:سُوٓءُ}} ({{tr:sūʾu}}) is the passive subject, the grammar says the evil itself was adorned; it does not become neutral. The later seeing as good shows the overlay becoming a false verdict. The active-voice variant and the doubled sound sharpen the hidden-agent pressure without replacing the base passive.

topics.headline: hidden-agent passive beautification
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the beautifier is not named, while the deceptive appearance itself is foregrounded.
topics.reason: The Form II passive supports intensified made-beautiful presentation with suppressed agency.

topics.headline: evil remains the adorned subject
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the badness is grammatically what gets adorned, not something morally reclassified by the narrator.
topics.reason: QAC and local syntax identify the following badness phrase as passive subject.

topics.headline: beautification becomes judgment
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices a chain from attractive surface to mistaken moral judgment.
topics.reason: The word stands before the seeing verb and is resumed by the object pronoun there.

topics.headline: variant agency and compact sound
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that variant and sound evidence sharpen the hidden-agent pressure without replacing the base passive reading.
topics.reason: The active variant is apparatus-level contrast; the local canonical form remains passive.

words.gloss_range: preposition-plus-suffix marking the deluded person’s affected viewpoint
words.prose: {{ar:لَهُۥ}} ({{tr:lahu}}) localizes the beautification in his frame: for him, to him, or in his view. The same suffixal referent receives the beautification, owns the deed, and then sees it, so the clause traps reception, possession, and evaluation inside one self-referential circuit. Its placement before the badness is named lets the distorted viewpoint appear before the underlying evil is exposed.

topics.headline: beautification localized to his view
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the apparent beauty belongs to the person’s evaluative frame, not to the deed as objective improvement.
topics.reason: The lām phrase attaches to the passive verb and marks affected viewpoint.

topics.headline: one pronoun circuit
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the same human subject receives, owns, and judges the deed.
topics.reason: The suffix chain returns repeatedly to the same referent.

topics.headline: viewpoint before badness
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the phrase delays the named evil by first locating distortion in the receiver’s perspective.
topics.reason: The preposition-suffix unit intervenes between the passive verb and its subject.

words.gloss_range: construct head naming badness as the governing quality of the deed
words.root_gloss_range: range of evil, harm, ugliness, shame, and distress; locally the badness is the reality reversed by appraisal
words.prose: {{ar:سُوٓءُ}} ({{tr:sūʾu}}) leads the construct phrase, so badness is the grammatical and moral category under which the deed appears. Its field of harm, ugliness, and repulsion makes the later {{ar:حَسَنًۭا}} ({{tr:ḥasanan}}) a real reversal, not a mild change of tone. The ayah lets the distorted viewpoint arrive first, but then names evil as the subject being beautified and as the reality against which the perceived good will collide.

topics.headline: badness as construct head
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the deed is introduced under the category of badness before any self-appraisal occurs.
topics.reason: The nominative construct head governs the following deed noun.

topics.headline: badness against perceived good
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices a moral inversion: the term of repulsion is processed by the subject as beauty and goodness.
topics.reason: The lexical opposition with the later complement is locally explicit.

topics.headline: evil deed after righteous action field
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that action remains central across the boundary, but its true valuation is now contested.
topics.reason: The local and same-surah action fields support this as a moral-evaluation network.

words.gloss_range: possessed deed as enacted work and domain of badness
words.root_gloss_range: range of work, deed, practice, and produced conduct; locally an owned enacted deed misread by its doer
words.prose: {{ar:عَمَلِهِۦ}} ({{tr:ʿamalihi}}) makes the evil concrete as his own enacted work. The genitive construct keeps the deed as the domain qualified by badness, while the suffix prevents the case from drifting into abstract evil detached from agency. The same possessor later sees it, so ownership and appraisal fuse into self-protective judgment; by the close, the opening deed is widened into what they craft under divine knowledge. The same-surah contrast with righteous work that ascends (35:10) keeps this misread deed inside a broader work-accounting frame.

topics.headline: owned enacted work
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the misread object is conduct the person has actually produced and owns.
topics.reason: The genitive noun and suffix tie badness to the person’s enacted work.

topics.headline: owner becomes evaluator
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the doer judges his own work, exposing the self-protective nature of the appraisal.
topics.reason: The same pronoun is tied to ownership and to the later perception verb.

topics.headline: work field across ayah and surah
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices a wider work-accounting frame: personal deed here, righteous work in 35:10, and crafted products at the close.
topics.reason: The cited same-surah and cross-reference fields link work to moral accounting and misjudgment.

words.gloss_range: result fa binding beautification to seeing inside the relative clause
words.prose: {{ar:فَ}} ({{tr:fa}}) keeps the two perfect verbs ordered inside the human type: beautification comes first, then seeing it as good follows. The connector prevents the verbs from becoming a flat list and denies the viewer’s judgment the status of independent insight. The second verb is grammatically downstream from the attractive presentation.

topics.headline: seeing as result of beautification
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the false seeing is a consequence of beautification, not a freestanding act of insight.
topics.reason: The fa remains inside the relative clause and links the two verbs sequentially.

words.gloss_range: seeing verb functioning as evaluative deeming with the evil deed as object
words.root_gloss_range: range of seeing, perceiving, considering, and judging; locally selected as evaluative perception
words.prose: {{ar:رَءَاهُ}} ({{tr:raʾāhu}}) turns sight into judgment. With {{ar:حَسَنًۭا}} ({{tr:ḥasanan}}) as complement, the verb means he deemed it good, while the object suffix carries the same evil deed inside the perception verb. The perfect sequence makes the distortion feel already settled: the dressed object has hardened into a moral verdict in the subject’s own perception. The evaluative-seeing echo (107:1) and the sharp glottal break further mark the verb as a moral-judgment pivot.

topics.headline: seeing as deeming
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the verb describes moral appraisal, not eyesight alone.
topics.reason: The complement selects the judgment sense within the seeing range.

topics.headline: evil deed carried as object
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the object has not changed; only the subject’s apprehension has changed.
topics.reason: The object suffix resumes the earlier bad deed phrase.

topics.headline: settled misvaluation chain
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the completed psychological chain, with evaluative-seeing echoes such as 107:1 sharpening the moral judgment frame.
topics.reason: The perfect sequence and cited evaluative seeing reference support a completed appraisal chain.

words.gloss_range: accusative quality assigned by perception, not certified moral reality
words.root_gloss_range: range joining beauty, goodness, approval, and excellence; locally narrowed to perceived goodness
words.prose: {{ar:حَسَنًۭا}} ({{tr:ḥasanan}}) lands as the value assigned by {{ar:رَءَاهُ}} ({{tr:raʾāhu}}). Its accusative, indefinite complement position keeps goodness inside appraisal rather than making it the deed’s certified reality. Because the root joins beauty and moral goodness, the ayah exploits the overlap: attractiveness masquerades as ethical rightness, unlike actual excellence commanded in 16:90.

topics.headline: goodness as assigned complement
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that goodness arrives after the seeing verb as an assigned predicate.
topics.reason: The accusative complement position keeps the quality inside the perception construction.

topics.headline: beauty-goodness overlap exploited
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices how a word that can carry beauty and goodness becomes the site of moral misclassification.
topics.reason: The local opposition with badness makes the aesthetic-ethical overlap decisive.

topics.headline: indefinite perceived good versus real excellence
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that perceived good is separated from real iḥsān, with 16:90 serving as a contrast.
topics.reason: The indefinite form and cited excellence passage support the contrast without replacing the local complement sense.

words.gloss_range: fa pivot from distorted case to emphatic divine explanation
words.prose: {{ar:فَ}} ({{tr:fa}}) before {{ar:إِنَّ}} ({{tr:inna}}) turns the opening case toward explanation. The connector itself does not govern the clause; it marks the move from corrupted perception to the divine agency frame that accounts for path outcomes. The ayah therefore does not leave misvaluation as psychology alone.

topics.headline: case-to-doctrine pivot
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the false appraisal is immediately placed under a governing divine frame.
topics.reason: The bound fa introduces the explanatory inna-clause while inna governs the syntax.

words.gloss_range: emphatic particle installing the divine path-governance clause
words.prose: {{ar:إِنَّ}} ({{tr:inna}}) makes the divine agency clause emphatic, not tentative. It governs the divine name and holds both path predicates in one asserted frame, so misguidance and guidance are explained together rather than by separate standards. The emphasis answers the resistance that false self-assessment might produce.

topics.headline: emphatic divine agency clause
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that one emphatic clause contains both opposite path outcomes under God.
topics.reason: Inna governs the nominal clause and spans the two following predicates.

words.gloss_range: proper divine name as one subject over opposite path outcomes
words.root_gloss_range: proper divine name; locally the named subject of guidance and misguidance
words.prose: {{ar:ٱللَّهَ}} ({{tr:llāha}}) becomes the explicit subject before both path verbs. The proper name prevents the explanation from becoming impersonal causality or mere psychology: the same named God governs misguidance and guidance on the path-axis evoked by the guidance frame (1:6-7). This subject also returns at the close, bracketing the restraint on grief between divine agency and divine knowledge.

topics.headline: one subject over both outcomes
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that opposite path outcomes are placed under one named divine subject.
topics.reason: The divine name is the ism of inna and precedes both predicates.

topics.headline: path frame and later bracket
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the path-axis connection to 1:6-7 and the repeated divine-name bracket around grief.
topics.reason: The cited guidance frame and later repetition support a broader path-governance bracket.

words.gloss_range: Form IV misguiding verb naming caused path-loss under divine will
words.root_gloss_range: range of wandering, error, loss, and straying; locally causative path-loss paired with guidance
words.prose: {{ar:يُضِلُّ}} ({{tr:yuḍillu}}) names path-loss as a transitive outcome: the open human object is affected, and the following will-clause defines the selection. Its Form IV causative shape keeps the statement from being mere wandering, while the paired guidance verb sharpens the root into an exact path antithesis. The 1:7 echo helps the reader hear misguidance as a path category, not just an inner mistake.

topics.headline: causative path-loss
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that misguidance is presented as a caused outcome under divine disposal, not simple self-wandering.
topics.reason: The Form IV verb takes the following human object directly.

topics.headline: misguidance against guidance
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices a balanced path-axis where loss and guidance define each other.
topics.reason: The verb is paired with the guidance verb in the same syntax.

topics.headline: astray echo and compressed sound
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that 1:7 supplies path-category resonance while the local form remains the governing verb.
topics.reason: The echo supports the path category; sound evidence is ancillary but locally compatible.

words.gloss_range: object-relative pronoun opening the first divine-will selection frame
words.prose: {{ar:مَن}} ({{tr:man}}) is the object of {{ar:يُضِلُّ}} ({{tr:yuḍillu}}) and also opens the will clause. It keeps the human object open until {{ar:يَشَآءُ}} ({{tr:yashāʾu}}) completes the phrase, so selection is not decided by visible labels or self-appraisal. This first {{ar:مَن يَشَآءُ}} ({{tr:man yashāʾu}}) establishes the template that the guidance half will repeat.

topics.headline: open object completed by will
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the human object remains grammatically open until divine will closes the selection frame.
topics.reason: The pronoun fills the object slot and launches the relative clause.

words.gloss_range: imperfect divine willing that completes the first selection frame
words.root_gloss_range: range of willing and determining a thing; locally divine specification of the misguidance object
words.prose: {{ar:يَشَآءُ}} ({{tr:yashāʾu}}) completes the first selection frame with God as the implicit subject. The imperfect keeps divine willing active within the formula, and the root’s link with determinate thingness makes the open human object specified by God, not by the subject’s own estimate. Its exact repetition later will make divine will the shared variable in both outcomes.

topics.headline: active divine specification
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the object of misguidance is specified by divine will, not by human self-appraisal.
topics.reason: The imperfect verb follows the open object and has the divine name as implicit subject.

topics.headline: shared will variable prepared
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that this will verb is not isolated; it prepares exact repetition across the two path outcomes.
topics.reason: Same-surah and formulaic recurrence support a repeated will frame.

words.gloss_range: waw coordinating opposite divine predicates under one subject
words.prose: {{ar:وَ}} ({{tr:wa}}) adds the guidance predicate without introducing a new subject. The same divine name therefore governs both sides, and the connector makes the second verb a coordinated counterpart rather than a corrective afterthought. Coordination and contrast work together: one syntax holds the path opposites.

topics.headline: one-subject coordination of opposites
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that misguidance and guidance are coordinated as a balanced rule under one subject.
topics.reason: The waw joins the second predicate to the first while retaining the same subject.

words.gloss_range: direct transitive guidance completing the divine path antithesis
words.root_gloss_range: range of directing, showing, guiding, and wayfinding; locally direct divine orientation
words.prose: {{ar:يَهْدِى}} ({{tr:yahdī}}) completes the path pair. It takes {{ar:مَن}} ({{tr:man}}) directly, so guidance is not just route information but direct orientation of the person. Paired with {{ar:يُضِلُّ}} ({{tr:yuḍillu}}), it answers the distorted viewer’s self-made compass with true orientation under the same divine will. The Book-guidance field (2:2) remains a contrast: here God is the direct guide of the human object.

topics.headline: direct orientation of the person
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that guidance acts directly on the person, not merely on a path sign.
topics.reason: The verb takes the relative pronoun as direct object.

topics.headline: guidance completes path-axis
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that guidance is defined here as the exact opposite of path-loss under one balanced syntax.
topics.reason: The verb mirrors the misguidance verb in tense and object frame.

topics.headline: Book-guidance field and divine guide
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that Quranic guidance vocabulary is present, but the local clause presents God as the direct guide.
topics.reason: The 2:2 reference is useful contrast while local transitivity controls the sense.

words.gloss_range: second object-relative pronoun mirroring the first selection frame
words.prose: {{ar:مَن}} ({{tr:man}}) repeats the object role after guidance. The repeated {{ar:مَن يَشَآءُ}} ({{tr:man yashāʾu}}) gives the second outcome the same syntactic selection frame as the first, so opposite meanings are held by matching grammar. The symmetry blocks reading guidance by a different standard from misguidance.

topics.headline: mirrored object and will phrase
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the guided object receives the same syntactic template as the misguided object.
topics.reason: The pronoun is direct object of the guidance verb and repeats the selection phrase.

words.gloss_range: second divine willing closing the balanced path formula
words.root_gloss_range: range of willing and determining a thing; locally the repeated divine will governing guidance as well as loss
words.prose: {{ar:يَشَآءُ}} ({{tr:yashāʾu}}) closes the balanced formula. Its subject remains God, so the guided do not become the source of the decisive will. Exact repetition after both outcomes makes divine will the common variable; misguidance and guidance are not to be read by different standards, a logic echoed by 18:17.

topics.headline: same will governs guidance
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that guidance, like misguidance, is governed by the same divine will formula.
topics.reason: The repeated verb has the same implicit divine subject and closes the pair.

topics.headline: 18:17 path-governance echo
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that 18:17 supports the same pairing of guidance and misguidance under God.
topics.reason: The echo confirms the path-governance frame without controlling the local parse.

words.gloss_range: fa turning divine path doctrine into a prohibition on grief-driven self-loss
words.prose: {{ar:فَ}} ({{tr:fa}}) moves from doctrine to response. Because path outcomes are under divine will, the addressee is not told to numb concern but to stop grief from consuming his own self. The connector formally launches the prohibition from the preceding divine-agency statement and turns moral explanation into disciplined self-limitation.

topics.headline: divine doctrine becomes self-restraint
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the prohibition follows from divine will, not from denial that the deluded person’s state matters.
topics.reason: The fa introduces the prohibitive jussive sequence as a consequence of the prior clause.

words.gloss_range: prohibitive lā scoping over the whole self-loss scene
words.prose: {{ar:لَا}} ({{tr:lā}}) is prohibitive with the jussive verb, so the self’s going-away is forbidden rather than merely reported as absent. Its scope covers the motion verb, the addressed self, the people over whom grief gathers, and the plural griefs. The command restrains self-consuming sorrow while leaving concern itself intact.

topics.headline: prohibition over self-loss and griefs
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the command blocks the whole affective sequence of self-depletion over them.
topics.reason: The particle governs the jussive verb and scopes over the following phrase.

words.gloss_range: jussive going-away verb picturing grief as self-depletion
words.root_gloss_range: range of going away, vanishing, removal, and departure; locally prohibited self-loss under grief
words.prose: {{ar:تَذْهَبْ}} ({{tr:tadhhab}}) gives grief a motion image: the self is in danger of going away. The jussive form after {{ar:لَا}} ({{tr:lā}}) makes the movement checked by prohibition, and the base reading makes {{ar:نَفْسُكَ}} ({{tr:nafsuka}}) the departing subject. The ten-reading causative variant sharpens the danger without replacing the base image: grief can carry the self away, and the addressee can be involved in causing that loss. The same-surah removal field (35:16) contrasts divine taking-away with the prohibited spending of the self in grief.

topics.headline: jussive self-departure image
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices grief pictured as the addressee’s own presence and capacity going away.
topics.reason: The base verb is jussive after prohibitive lā and takes the self as subject.

topics.headline: causative reading sharpens self-loss
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that an accepted reading adds a causative angle to the danger of self-loss, while the base reading still governs the local prose.
topics.reason: The ten-reading changes form and case, so it is valid contrast but not a replacement for the base parse.

topics.headline: self-loss limited after divine will
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that responsibility is limited: divine path governance is followed by a command not to spend the self in grief.
topics.reason: The motion verb organizes the prohibited scene and same-surah recurrence sharpens the going-away field.

words.gloss_range: addressed possessed self endangered by grief
words.root_gloss_range: range of self, soul, person, and breath; locally the addressee’s own life-bearing self
words.prose: {{ar:نَفْسُكَ}} ({{tr:nafsuka}}) makes the prohibition personal: it is your self that must not be spent over them. The root field of self, soul, person, and breath turns grief into life-pressure, not a tidy emotion. In the base reading the self is the departing subject; in the variant it becomes the object caused to vanish, so both grammars intensify the need to guard the addressee’s own self from depletion.

topics.headline: your singular self at stake
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the doctrine about others becomes a direct constraint on the addressee’s own self.
topics.reason: The singular possessed noun binds the threatened self to the second-person addressee.

topics.headline: subject or object across readings
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that variant case shifts the self’s grammatical role while preserving the same self-loss danger.
topics.reason: The base reading is nominative subject; the variant is accusative object.

topics.headline: breathing self under affective limit
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the endangered self is life-bearing and morally accountable, not an abstract psychological label.
topics.reason: Root range and same-surah/cross-reference evidence support life and moral responsibility associations.

topics.headline: your self set against them
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the boundary between the addressee’s self and the group over whom grief gathers.
topics.reason: Word order and the following prepositional phrase make the contrast visible.

words.gloss_range: preposition-plus-plural suffix giving grief its target without making that group controllers
words.prose: {{ar:عَلَيْهِمْ}} ({{tr:ʿalayhim}}) gives the grief its object or cause: over them, on account of them. The burden-preposition lets concern be real without making the group controllers of the addressee’s self. Its placement between {{ar:نَفْسُكَ}} ({{tr:nafsuka}}) and {{ar:حَسَرَٰتٍ}} ({{tr:ḥasarātin}}) channels the threatened self-loss toward a specific group before the griefs are named.

topics.headline: concern target without control
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that grief has a target, but that target does not own the addressee’s self.
topics.reason: The prepositional phrase attaches to the motion/prohibition scene and marks object or cause.

topics.headline: phrase mediates self and griefs
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices how the wording routes the self-loss toward them before naming the plural griefs.
topics.reason: The phrase stands between the addressed self and the final grief noun.

words.gloss_range: indefinite plural griefs as the manner and pressure of prohibited self-loss
words.root_gloss_range: range of regret, exposure, stripping, weariness, and exhaustion; locally accumulating grief states
words.prose: {{ar:حَسَرَٰتٍ}} ({{tr:ḥasarātin}}) names the affective medium after the self, target, and motion have been set. The indefinite plural makes grief repeated and unbounded, not a single contained sorrow. Its root field of regret, stripping, and weariness makes the danger more than sentiment: grief can expose and exhaust capacity, while the 36:30 regret echo sharpens the loss-field that the addressee is forbidden to inhabit. The tanwīn cadence links false valuation, plural grief, and final knowledge, and the rare abstract plural makes the sorrow feel distributionally heavy.

topics.headline: unbounded plural griefs
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the prohibition concerns accumulating griefs as the medium and pressure of self-loss.
topics.reason: The indefinite plural can function circumstantially or causally in the prohibition scene.

topics.headline: regret as stripping exhaustion
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices grief as capacity-stripping exhaustion, not emotion alone.
topics.reason: The root range supports regret, exposure, stripping, and weariness as locally relevant pressure.

topics.headline: 36:30 regret echo and final cadence
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the regret cry-field from 36:30 and the marked plural cadence at the close of the prohibition.
topics.reason: The echo and distribution/sound rows add secondary but real payoff without changing grammar.

words.gloss_range: final inna opening an emphatic knowledge clause that grounds restraint
words.prose: {{ar:إِنَّ}} ({{tr:inna}}) opens the final grounding clause. After the prohibition, it does not merely add information; it asserts the reason restraint can hold: God’s knowledge stands where consuming grief must not. The particle launches a stable nominal assertion that shifts closure from human sorrow to divine awareness.

topics.headline: final emphatic ground of restraint
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the closing knowledge claim grounds restraint rather than functioning as detached description.
topics.reason: The second inna governs the final nominal clause after the prohibition.

words.gloss_range: repeated divine name anchoring final knowledge in the same God who governs paths
words.root_gloss_range: proper divine name; locally the named subject of final knowledge
words.prose: {{ar:ٱللَّهَ}} ({{tr:llāha}}) returns instead of letting a pronoun carry the clause. The same named God who governs path outcomes now knows what they craft, so agency and knowledge bracket the addressee’s grief. The proper name makes the closing knowledge personal and authoritative, not an abstract principle. The teaching-and-knowing field (2:282) supports this as named divine knowledge over crafted acts.

topics.headline: same divine subject returns
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the closure visibly recenters on the named God after the grief prohibition.
topics.reason: The divine name is repeated as the ism of the final inna.

topics.headline: agency and knowledge bracket grief
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the bracket: God governs paths in the middle and knows crafted acts at the end.
topics.reason: The repeated name links the middle agency clause to the final knowledge clause.

topics.headline: authoritative knowing subject
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the knowledge claim is named divine knowledge over crafted acts, with 2:282 as a supporting knowledge-teaching field.
topics.reason: The cross-reference supports divine knowledge authority without adding a new local sense.

words.gloss_range: stable intensive knowledge predicate answering flawed seeing and grief
words.root_gloss_range: range of knowing, marking, and making known; locally stable divine knowledge of crafted acts
words.prose: {{ar:عَلِيمٌ}} ({{tr:ʿalīmun}}) gives the closure a stable predicate of knowledge, not an event of discovering. Its intensive pattern and final position make divine knowledge answer both the opening false seeing and the grief that follows. With the governed phrase about what they craft, the knowledge reaches produced conduct that beautified self-appraisal cannot hide. The knowledge field that includes divinely taught names (2:31) and same-surah closures stays locally tethered to these crafted acts.

topics.headline: stable intensive knowledge
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that knowledge is presented as an enduring divine attribute, not a one-time report.
topics.reason: The faʿīl predicate in a nominal clause supports stable intensive force.

topics.headline: knowledge reaches crafted conduct
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that divine knowledge reaches the deliberate products humans craft and may beautify to themselves.
topics.reason: The following governed phrase names the domain of crafted acts.

topics.headline: flawed seeing answered by divine knowing
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the epistemic arc from corrupted human seeing to stable divine knowledge.
topics.reason: The final predicate closes the ayah against the earlier perception verb.

topics.headline: same-surah and 2:31 knowledge field
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the knowledge vocabulary belongs to a larger divine knowledge field while remaining locally tied to crafted acts.
topics.reason: The echoes support the closure field without changing the local predicate.

words.gloss_range: prepositional bi attaching the knowledge predicate to its object-domain
words.prose: {{ar:بِ}} ({{tr:bi}}) tethers {{ar:عَلِيمٌ}} ({{tr:ʿalīmun}}) to a concrete domain. It marks what divine knowledge is about, not an instrument by which God knows. Fused to the following relative pronoun, it keeps the final attribute from floating as a general abstraction and attaches it directly to what they craft.

topics.headline: domain marker for knowledge
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the knowledge predicate is immediately tied to the specific object-domain of their production.
topics.reason: The preposition connects the predicate to the relative clause as its governed domain.

words.gloss_range: relative mā opening the broad content clause of what they craft
words.prose: {{ar:مَا}} ({{tr:mā}}) opens the content under divine knowledge. Governed by {{ar:بِ}} ({{tr:bi}}) and completed only by {{ar:يَصْنَعُونَ}} ({{tr:yaṣnaʿūn}}), it keeps the object broad enough for acts, schemes, products, and outcomes. The object of knowledge is delayed until the crafting verb defines it.

topics.headline: broad relative object of knowledge
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that divine knowledge covers whatever they craft, not only a narrow named act.
topics.reason: The relative pronoun is governed by the preposition and completed by the final verb.

words.gloss_range: imperfect plural craft verb closing human production under divine knowledge
words.root_gloss_range: range of skilled making, fashioning, crafting, and deliberate production; locally ongoing collective human crafting
words.prose: {{ar:يَصْنَعُونَ}} ({{tr:yaṣnaʿūn}}) gives the ayah its final human verb, but it lands under divine knowledge rather than under the makers’ self-appraisal. The imperfect plural presents ongoing collective production, and the craft root exceeds generic doing by suggesting deliberate shaped output. The opening personal deed is now widened into what they craft, so the close exposes made human products to a knower beyond the makers; the 20:41 contrast keeps divine fashioning distinct from this human crafting.

topics.headline: ongoing collective makers
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the close names ongoing collective production, not a single completed private act.
topics.reason: The imperfect plural form carries ongoing aspect and plural actors.

topics.headline: craft beyond generic doing
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices deliberate workmanship or contrivance rather than generic doing.
topics.reason: The ṣ-n-ʿ field and Form I local verb select crafted making.

topics.headline: human craft under divine knowledge
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the ayah ends on what humans make as known by God, not on their own beautified appraisal.
topics.reason: The final verb completes the relative clause governed by the knowledge predicate.

topics.headline: personal deed widened to collective craft
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the bookend from one person’s deed to collective crafted production, with 20:41 contrasting divine fashioning.
topics.reason: Opening deed and closing craft rows support the widening frame; the cross-reference is contrastive.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: The opening sequence moves from beautification to a bad intended act, then to seeing it as good.
baseline_models.mechanism: A change in presentation precedes a change in perception, and perception then supplies an inverted value judgment. The verse therefore depicts a self-confirming appraisal loop rather than merely placing a bad deed beside an unrelated mistaken opinion.

activation_trace.role: The branch supplies the making-visible of goodness and functions as the surface-changing first step.
The branch supplies objective ugliness or badness, preserving the gap between the act and its appearance.
The branch supplies purposive action, so the object being misread is enacted conduct rather than a free-floating idea.
The branch joins sensory and inward seeing, making perception the hinge between display and evaluation.
The branch supplies desirability opposed to ugliness and completes the evaluative reversal.

changed_reading.before: A person simply mistakes an evil deed for a good one.
changed_reading.after: The verse traces how a treated surface recruits perception and turns perception into a verdict that contradicts the act's character.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: The paired divine actions of misdirecting and guiding are followed by a prohibition against letting the self go away over others.
baseline_models.mechanism: Misdirection can be deviation, disappearance, or loss, while guidance can be gentle indication, orientation, or a leading front. The later motion verb extends this path field to the observer: another's lost route must not cause the observer's own self to depart from its course.

activation_trace.role: The branch supplies deviation from a path or aim and establishes the negative trajectory.
The branch supplies disappearance from view, allowing misdirection also to be a loss of perceptual availability.
The branch supplies gentle indication toward a road or truth and establishes the positive trajectory.
The branch supplies a guide or leading edge that goes ahead, giving guidance a spatially directional shape.
The branch supplies going and passing away, transferring route language to the addressed self.

changed_reading.before: Guidance and misguidance name settled religious categories, followed by a separate consolation.
changed_reading.after: The ayah presents competing trajectories of orientation, loss, and departure, then warns that grief can pull the witness into a second departure.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: The self is prohibited from going over them in plural regrets.
baseline_models.mechanism: Regret over what is lost can shade into exhaustion and exhausted looking. Coupled with the self as life and inward discernment, the clause protects the perceiving, living subject from being spent across repeated objects of grief.

activation_trace.role: The branch supplies passing away and makes the threatened cost the self's own depletion or departure.
The branch supplies the life-bearing self, raising the stakes beyond a transient mood.
The branch supplies inward reason and intention, so grief also threatens the faculty that reads the situation.
The branch supplies spent strength and fatigued sight, converting regret into an attritional mechanism.
The branch supplies grief over what has escaped, retaining the clause's direct affective sense.

changed_reading.before: The addressee is told not to feel excessive sorrow.
changed_reading.after: The command safeguards life and discernment from a repetitive grief process that can consume the one who sees others' misreading.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: The ayah opens with a passive beautification and closes with knowledge of what people actively fashion.
baseline_models.mechanism: The frame moves from a received attractive display to purposive work and finally to making, including affected self-presentation. It leaves agency layered: a person may receive a misleading appearance and also participate in maintaining or manufacturing it.

activation_trace.role: The branch supplies an appearance made good and marks the passive, presented side of the frame.
The branch supplies intended action and prevents the displayed object from being treated as morally inert.
The branch supplies active making and closes the ayah on production rather than appearance alone.
The branch supplies affected refinement and self-adornment, creating a direct functional echo with the opening display.
The branch supplies disclosure to the knower, opposing the actor's surface-bound verdict.

changed_reading.before: An unspecified agent decorates a deed, while God later knows unrelated actions.
changed_reading.after: The beginning and end form an appearance-production frame in which received deception and human maintenance of the display can coexist.

context_deltas.mechanism: The attractive surface becomes socially transmissible: unstable glitter deceives, a call inclines hearers, and a faction consolidates them around a shared position. The focus appraisal loop can therefore recruit and stabilize a group rather than remaining private.

activation_trace.role: The focus branch supplies the attractive display that becomes the content of recruitment.
The focus branch supplies an inward opinion, the private verdict that social reinforcement can stabilize.
The context branch supplies deception by what gleams without holding, specifying how beautification can mislead.
The context branch supplies a verbal call that inclines others, carrying the appraisal outward.
The context branch supplies a group organized around an opinion, giving the deception social persistence.

structural_cues: 35:5 repeats the deception root around worldly life and relation to God.
35:6 sequences enemy, invitation, faction, and destination immediately before the focus ayah.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies glitter-deception, inclination by calling, and opinion-based grouping; I infer a recruitment chain from private appraisal to collective reinforcement. A live alternative is that the warnings remain parallel rather than causally sequential.

changed_reading.before: The mistaken judgment belongs to an isolated individual.
changed_reading.after: A polished misjudgment can be called, shared, and consolidated until a group helps each member keep seeing it as good.

context_deltas.mechanism: The context repeatedly presents visibility with a causal history: stirring produces cloud movement and revived land; water produces ripe fruit and acquired colors; visible variation culminates in knowledge. The focus problem is thus not beauty or sight as such, but an attractive verdict severed from a truth-producing sequence.

activation_trace.role: The focus branch supplies displayed goodness whose provenance is under examination.
The focus branch supplies the desirable verdict that can be either warranted or counterfeit.
The context branch supplies a visible process stirred from one state into another, beginning a traceable causal chain.
The context branch supplies actual land-life through rain and growth, a material result rather than cosmetic display.
The context branch supplies ripe fruit as an inspectable outcome of the preceding water process.
The context branch supplies acquisition of color, making visible difference a produced state rather than bare decoration.
The context branch supplies knowledgeable disclosure, showing a route from observed variation to a calibrated response.

structural_cues: 35:27 begins with a demand to see and follows water through fruit and color; 35:28 follows with knowledgeable fear.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies generated life, fruit, color, seeing, and knowledge; I infer that warranted beauty is beauty with recoverable provenance. A live alternative is that these natural sequences illustrate power without setting an epistemic test for 35:8.

changed_reading.before: Visible attractiveness is itself epistemically suspect.
changed_reading.after: The ayah criticizes beauty detached from the real process and consequences of an act, while leaving causally legible beauty as a valid sign.

context_deltas.mechanism: The later unequal pairs separate raw sensory possession from inward capacity: one may visually register an attractive object while remaining inwardly blind or unresponsive. The focus seeing is therefore compatible with a failure of insight.

activation_trace.role: The focus branch spans eye and insight, leaving open which kind of seeing has succeeded.
The focus branch supplies the attractive verdict generated by incomplete seeing.
The context branch supplies blindness of inward perception, allowing outward sight and failed judgment to coexist.
The context branch supplies insight of the heart as the missing comparator to surface recognition.
The context branch supplies illumination, giving correct perception an enabling medium beyond the appealing object.
The context branch supplies understanding and responsive compliance, extending perception from reception to answerability.

structural_cues: 35:19-22 presents a chain of non-equivalences: blind and seeing, darkness and light, living and dead.
35:22 repeats causing-to-hear and inability to make hear around divine willing.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies explicit contrasts among blindness, insight, illumination, and responsive hearing; I infer that the focus actor's seeing is a counterfeit completion of perception. A live alternative is that the contrast classifies people without analyzing the earlier perceptual verb.

changed_reading.before: The actor sees accurately but applies the wrong moral label.
changed_reading.after: The attractive sight may itself be perceptually incomplete: ocular or imaginal recognition has occurred without insight, illumination, or responsive hearing.

context_deltas.mechanism: The context denies transfer of another's load and makes self-directed purification accrue to that self. The focus command thus sets an ethical boundary: concern may remain, but the addressee must not convert others' misdirection into a burden that consumes his own self.

activation_trace.role: The focus branch supplies the person's own whole self as the entity whose boundary is protected.
The focus branch supplies exhaustion, the cost of trying to carry what cannot be transferred.
The context branch supplies the heavy load whose non-transfer is stated repeatedly.
The context branch supplies the condition of being burdened and makes the attempted transfer concrete.
The context branch supplies carrying a moral load, connecting affective overextension to responsibility.
The context branch returns purification to one's own self and closes the responsibility boundary.

structural_cues: 35:18 first denies one bearer carrying another's load, then denies relief even when a burdened person calls.
The same ayah says self-purification is for one's own self.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies non-transferable weight and self-indexed purification; I infer that grief can become an illicit simulation of carrying another's responsibility. A live alternative is that 35:18 concerns judgment only and does not regulate the affective burden in 35:8.

changed_reading.before: The prohibition merely limits emotional intensity.
changed_reading.after: It also protects the boundary of responsibility: compassion cannot become an attempt to bear another person's path or verdict.

context_deltas.mechanism: Actions are given trajectories independent of the actor's appraisal: good speech ascends, sound work raises it, corrupt planning perishes, and bad planning circles down upon its own people along a recurrent way. Calling an act good cannot redirect what the act actually does.

activation_trace.role: The focus branch supplies purposive action as the moving object whose trajectory can be tested.
The focus branch supplies the actor's opinion, which the context distinguishes from action's actual motion.
The context branch supplies upward movement as one objective trajectory.
The context branch supplies raising by sound action, joining value to effective motion.
The context branch supplies ruin and corruption as the contrary trajectory of bad planning.
The context branch supplies badness descending upon and enclosing its producers, making consequence reflexive.
The context branch supplies a recurrent way, extending a single act into a stable course with repeatable consequences.

structural_cues: 35:10 contrasts the upward sequence of good speech and sound work with the perishing of bad planning.
35:43 states that bad planning encloses its own people and repeats the language of an unchanging way.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies opposed motions and reflexive consequence; I infer that these motions are an audit of the focus actor's value judgment. A live alternative is that ascent and encirclement concern reward and punishment without describing an intrinsic action trajectory.

changed_reading.before: The central problem is an incorrect label attached to a deed.
changed_reading.after: The deed's real direction persists beneath the label: sound action rises, while polished corruption still decays and returns upon its makers.

context_deltas.mechanism: The closing knowledge clause is expanded inward: contextual knowledge reaches the hidden, and the chest is presented as the origin from which actions issue. The apparent passive display can therefore be traced into an interior workshop of intention, interpretation, and active self-fashioning without settling the passive agent.

activation_trace.role: The focus branch supplies the outwardly improved display whose source remains initially hidden.
The focus branch supplies affected self-presentation, connecting inward production to outward attractiveness.
The focus branch supplies full disclosure to the knower and anchors the closing audit.
The context branch supplies knowledge of a report's inner reality, moving the audit beneath presentation.
The context branch supplies what is screened from eyes, the domain inaccessible to the focus actor's surface judgment.
The context branch supplies an interior source from which actions emerge, locating the workshop behind display.
The context branch repeats disclosure across both hidden worlds and inner selves, completing the depth contrast.

structural_cues: 35:31 pairs divine expertise with sight concerning servants.
35:38 moves from knowledge of the unseen cosmos to knowledge of what is within chests.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies hidden depth, inner origin, making, and affected presentation; I infer a production line from interior stance to outwardly beautified action. A live alternative is that the closing making verb denotes deeds generally and does not imply self-fashioning.

changed_reading.before: The final clause only assures that outward deeds are observed.
changed_reading.after: It answers the opening illusion with depth knowledge: the whole hidden production of an attractive moral surface is already exposed.

context_deltas.mechanism: A group claims it would be better guided, yet arrival of warning increases its recoil; pride then sustains bad planning until the plan encloses its owners. Misdirection can thus be an active counter-movement under contact with guidance, not merely lack of information.

activation_trace.role: The focus branch supplies deviation, now tested as a response rather than a static location.
The focus branch supplies gentle indication toward truth, the contact against which recoil occurs.
The context branch supplies an explicit claim to superior guidance and makes the later response diagnostic.
The context branch supplies increase, turning exposure to warning into intensification rather than correction.
The context branch supplies recoil and distancing, the enacted direction of resistance.
The context branch supplies self-greatness and pride as a motive that can protect the beautified verdict.
The context branch supplies enclosing return, the eventual shape of the recoil-driven course.

structural_cues: 35:42 places a claim to greater guidance before the arrival of warning, then states that arrival increased recoil.
35:43 continues directly with pride, bad planning, and that planning's return upon its people.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies claimed openness, actual warning, increased recoil, pride, and reflexive consequence; I infer a defensive response loop that protects the attractive self-verdict. A live alternative is that recoil is simple rejection without dependence on the earlier beautification mechanism.

changed_reading.before: Misguidance is chiefly informational absence or a wrong route already taken.
changed_reading.after: It may be maintained as active recoil: contact with guidance threatens a pride-bearing attractive verdict and can intensify movement away.

context_deltas.mechanism: The context replaces snapshot appraisal with travel, deliberate looking, aftermath, earning, residual trace, and appointed delay. An act that looks good now must be read through the path it travels and what remains when its term arrives.

activation_trace.role: The focus branch supplies the immediate opinion that the temporal audit reopens.
The focus branch supplies apparent desirability at the initial viewing point.
The context branch supplies a traversed way or conduct, extending appraisal across a course.
The context branch supplies directed sight and insight as a deliberate audit rather than passive impression.
The context branch supplies the end-state and consequence that corrects the initial attractive snapshot.
The context branch supplies acquired return from action, linking conduct to what it actually yields.
The context branch supplies a remaining trace, making aftermath available even when the actor's moment has passed.
The context branch supplies an appointed temporal limit and explains why consequence may not be immediately visible.
The context branch supplies comprehensive seeing at the end of the delayed audit.

structural_cues: 35:44 commands movement through the land and looking at earlier peoples' aftermath.
35:45 connects earning to delayed reckoning at an appointed term and closes with divine sight.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies travel, inspection, aftermath, earned result, residue, and delay; I infer that duration is a test of the focus judgment. A live alternative is that the final historical command proves power rather than furnishing a method for evaluating deeds.

changed_reading.before: The actor's present experience of the deed as good is the only perceptual scene.
changed_reading.after: The verse's false sight is temporally myopic; adequate sight follows the deed through its course, residue, and delayed end.

context_deltas.mechanism: Repeated going-away language creates an affective reversal: persons can be removed, but the fulfilled speakers later praise the removal of sorrow and inhabit a state without exhausting toil. The focus prohibition can be heard as refusing to let grief perform removal upon the grieving self.

activation_trace.role: The focus branch supplies the self's threatened passing away under grief.
The focus branch supplies depletion of strength and sight as the means by which grief removes the self.
The context branch supplies removal of persons and makes going-away a consequential action, not only motion.
The context branch reverses the object of removal: sorrow, rather than the self, is made to pass away.
The context branch supplies grief as roughness within the self, the burden eventually removed.
The context branch supplies toil that wears a person down and clarifies the depletion avoided.
The context branch supplies weakness and fatigue as the terminal state absent from the promised dwelling.

structural_cues: 35:16 uses the same going root for the possible removal of people.
35:34-35 praises removal of sorrow and immediately denies both wearing toil and fatigue.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies removal of persons, removal of grief, and absence of exhaustion; I infer a contrast between grief removing the self and God removing grief. A live alternative is that the repeated root is only verbal recurrence and the passages do not form an affective reversal.

changed_reading.before: Do not go too far in feeling regret for them.
changed_reading.after: Do not let regret make your own self disappear; the desired reversal is that sorrow departs while the self remains unspent.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This is surprising because it uses the packet's non-dominant mapping of the seeing root to join deliberation with outward attractiveness. The exact focus occurrence and supplied split mapping keep it anchored, but downstream prose should call it a split-root heuristic, not claim that the focus verb is derived from the alternate root.
surprising_valid_outliers.focus_anchor: The focus seeing verb sits between prior beautification and the verdict of goodness.

activation_trace.role: The split branch supplies deliberation over an affair and suggests that the attractive verdict may be internally rehearsed.
The split branch supplies outward comeliness and links rehearsed opinion to an appealing view.
The focus branch supplies active improvement of appearance, the surface that reflection can keep polishing.
The focus branch supplies the desirable conclusion produced by the polished internal view.

changed_reading.before: The actor is passively fooled by a single attractive sight.
changed_reading.after: Exploratorily, repeated reflection may polish the view from within until a desired opinion presents itself as obvious sight.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This is branch-distant because it activates the non-dominant mapping of the guidance root as an unconfirmed image arising in the self. The packet explicitly supplies that mapping and the focus contains both guidance and self, so it remains traceable; downstream prose should present it only as a shadow reading beside ordinary guidance, never as its replacement.
surprising_valid_outliers.focus_anchor: The guidance verb is followed by a warning that the addressee's own self not depart over those who misread.

activation_trace.role: The dominant branch preserves guidance as gentle direction toward truth.
The split branch supplies an unratified inner image and functions as an exploratory shadow of failed orientation.
The focus branch locates thought, intention, and inward apprehension in the self that must be guarded.
The focus branch supplies the attractive force by which an unfixed inner image could gain conviction.

changed_reading.before: Guidance and misguidance concern only an externally described route.
changed_reading.after: As a contained shadow reading, orientation also concerns whether an inward image is gently fixed to truth or gains force merely by becoming attractive.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This is surprising because it spatializes regret as uncovering a concealed ugliness beneath decoration. Each element is directly anchored in a focus root, but the causal sequence is reader-supplied; downstream prose should say the roots can echo such an unmasking, not that the clause explicitly narrates it.
surprising_valid_outliers.focus_anchor: Decoration, concealed badness, seeing, and plural regrets all occur within the focus ayah.

activation_trace.role: The focus branch supplies a favorable surface laid over the act.
The focus branch supplies a shameful part ordinarily kept covered, giving badness a concealed underside.
The focus branch supplies removal of a covering and functions as the moment the polished surface is stripped away.
The focus branch retains regret over loss as the affect produced when the concealed reality becomes legible.

changed_reading.before: Regrets are only the observer's sadness about people who remain deceived.
changed_reading.after: The regrets can also echo repeated unmaskings: each attractive cover removed exposes the shame or loss that the initial sight concealed.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This is surprising because distant branches of the repeated willing root include attraction and being carried toward an affair. The exact repeated focus occurrence anchors the activation, but these branches must not redefine divine willing or collapse it into human desire; downstream prose should use them only to mark a contrastive field of attraction, compulsion, and sovereign willing.
surprising_valid_outliers.focus_anchor: The repeated willing construction stands between the attractive misreading and the command protecting the self.

activation_trace.role: The ordinary branch supplies willing related to bringing about or attaining a thing and keeps divine agency primary.
The distant branch supplies being carried or constrained toward an affair and adds an exploratory force-vector.
The distant branch supplies the self's attraction and delight in a thing, echoing the pull of apparent goodness.
The focus branch supplies the desirability that attracts the human perceiver before the repeated willing clause.

changed_reading.before: The repeated willing formula is wholly separate from the preceding attractive misreading.
changed_reading.after: Exploratorily, it interrupts a field of human captivation and compelled movement with sovereign willing, preventing apparent desirability from being mistaken for final control.

strongest_changes: The private appearance-to-verdict loop becomes a socially recruited and reinforced process.
Natural production sequences distinguish warranted visible goodness from cosmetic goodness without provenance.
Blindness, insight, illumination, and responsive hearing show that seeing an attractive object can still be failed perception.
Non-transferable burden turns the grief prohibition into a boundary of responsibility as well as an affective limit.
Action trajectories, hidden inward production, recoil under guidance, and delayed aftermath all audit the actor's present verdict.
summary.what_was_special: The focus ayah supports several simultaneous mechanisms: aesthetic inversion, path loss, social reinforcement, self-depletion, hidden self-fashioning, and temporal consequence. Its strangest live echoes come from split mappings that connect seeing with reflective polish and guidance with an unfixed inner image, plus the uncovering sense inside regret.
remaining_uncertainties: The passive agent of beautification remains unspecified in the focus ayah, and context does not force a single assignment.
The focus seeing may emphasize eyesight, inward opinion, or their collapse; the retained models should not disambiguate it prematurely.
The final making verb may denote deeds generally or active maintenance of a moral display.
The alternate mapped-root outliers are useful activation heuristics but remain form-distant and should be rendered with explicit qualification.

baseline.text: Kötü işi kendisine süslü gösterilen ve onu güzel gören kimse mi? Allah dilediğini saptırır, dilediğini doğru yola iletir. Onlar için duyduğun üzüntüler yüzünden kendini tüketme. Allah onların yaptıklarını bilir.

findings.text: Kötülük, dış görünüşü işlenip güzelleştirilen, sonra görülerek iyi diye değerlendirilen üretilmiş bir algı döngüsü içinde işler.
Başkalarının yönünü belirlemeye çalışmak, kişinin kendi canlı gücünü tüketen bir nedensellik yüküne dönüşebilir.
Üzüntü, onların yanıltıcı görünüşünü söküp açığa çıkarma çabasının tükenişi olarak da okunur ve bu görev ilahî bilgiye bırakılır.

inter_ayah_rows.note: It directly contrasts one upon clear proof with one whose evil deed is beautified and who follows desire.

inter_ayah_rows.label: weak
inter_ayah_rows.note: It distinguishes good and evil deeds in recompense but does not address evil being perceived as good.

inter_ayah_rows.label: medium
inter_ayah_rows.note: It links mistaken disbelief to abiding regret and closes with God's sight of what people do.

inter_ayah_rows.label: strong
inter_ayah_rows.note: It repeats the focus ayah's formulation that God misguides and guides whom He wills, with accountability for deeds.

inter_ayah_rows.note: Its discussion of unresponsive false gods does not materially clarify the focus relation.

inter_ayah_rows.label: strong
inter_ayah_rows.note: It explicitly says the disbelievers' evil deeds were beautified to them and associates that with misguidance.

inter_ayah_rows.label: strong
inter_ayah_rows.note: It joins beautified plotting, obstruction from the path, and the lack of a guide for one God misguides.

inter_ayah_rows.label: weak

channel_subchannels_anchored_here.parent_semantic_invariant: An intended form is brought into being and then stabilized as an artifact, inscription, rule, or record.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.parent_surprising_reach: Creation and writing converge as two kinds of form-making: one shapes beings, while the other arranges marks and makes an order durable.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.name: Origination as deliberate making
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.scene_or_process: An agent initiates, makes, and brings a formed entity into existence.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.active_motifs: making or producing a thing (quranic:root_000248:B001/m01); creative bringing-into-being (quranic:root_000434:B002/m01); performed manufacture (quranic:root_000885:B001/m01); origination and first emergence (quranic:root_001165:B002/m01)
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.ayah_anchors: 35:1 `فَاطِرِ/جَاعِلِ/خَلْقِ` (ف ط ر/ج ع ل/خ ل ق); 35:3 `خَٰلِقٍ` (خ ل ق); 35:8 `يَصْنَعُ` (ص ن ع); 35:11 `خَلَقَ/جَعَلَ` (خ ل ق/ج ع ل).
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.synthesis: The motifs distinguish initiation, fabrication, and emergence while keeping them in one production scene. Creation appears as the controlled establishment of form, not only as an abstract assertion of existence.

channel_subchannels_anchored_here.parent_semantic_invariant: Meaning moves from disclosure through perception into response, report, or distortion.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.parent_surprising_reach: The scene includes both receptive organs and communication logistics: insight opens an obstruction, news is broadcast, speech returns as an answer, and falsehood is a report diverted from its proper direction.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.name: Sight becoming inward knowledge
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.scene_or_process: A visible object is perceived, reflected upon, and penetrated until its inner condition becomes known.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.active_motifs: sight by eye or insight (quranic:root_000531:B001/m01); reflective judgment of the heart (quranic:root_000531:B002/m01); disclosure to the knower (quranic:root_001040:B001/m01); knowledge of a report's interior (quranic:root_000387:B001/m01); accurate wisdom (quranic:root_000348:B003/m01); opening an intellectual obstruction (quranic:root_001124:B008/m01)
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.synthesis: Seeing is not the endpoint. The scene moves from visual contact to reflection, accurate judgment, and knowledge of what lies beneath the report's exterior, with opening serving as the mechanism that makes insight possible.

channel_subchannels_anchored_here.parent_semantic_invariant: A surface controls how an entity appears, what it exposes, and what it protects.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.parent_surprising_reach: Appearance is grounded in craft and material layers: cosmetic display, armor, veil, hairy hide, leather container, and the stripping of flesh from bone.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.name: Crafted beauty and disfigurement
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.scene_or_process: A visible surface is judged, polished, or staged so that it appears attractive rather than defective.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.active_motifs: beauty opposed to ugliness (quranic:root_000323:B001/m01); ugliness and bad form (quranic:root_000755:B001/m01); beauty free of blemish (quranic:root_000660:B001/m01); active beautification (quranic:root_000660:B002/m01); self-fashioning and cosmetic display (quranic:root_000885:B004/m01); visible aspect and mirror-image (quranic:root_000531:B006/m01)
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.ayah_anchors: 35:8 `حَسَنًا/سُوٓءُ/زُيِّنَ/رَءَا/يَصْنَعُ` (ح س ن/س و ء/ز ي ن/ر ء ي/ص ن ع); 35:10 `سَّيِّـَٔاتِ` (س و ء); 35:12 `تَرَى` (ر ء ي).
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.synthesis: The scene distinguishes intrinsic appraisal, deliberate enhancement, and the beholder's visible impression. The beautified evil of 35:8 is therefore not merely misjudged; it is lexically compatible with a crafted presentation designed to manage the viewer.

channel_subchannels_anchored_here.parent_semantic_invariant: A surface controls how an entity appears, what it exposes, and what it protects.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.parent_surprising_reach: Appearance is grounded in craft and material layers: cosmetic display, armor, veil, hairy hide, leather container, and the stripping of flesh from bone.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.name: Hide converted into leather
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.scene_or_process: A marked animal surface loses hair or flesh, is stripped, and becomes a skin capable of holding contents.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.active_motifs: mark left on skin (quranic:root_000148:B006/m01); hide retaining hair during dressing (quranic:root_000844:B006/m01); skin that holds what is inside (quranic:root_001424:B005/m01); flesh stripped from bone (quranic:root_001348:B009/m01); shedding feather, hair, or old coat (quranic:root_000320:B005/m01)
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.synthesis: The surface becomes a worked material through shedding, stripping, and retention. This scene sharpens the distinction between living covering and manufactured container while keeping both within one conversion process.

channel_subchannels_anchored_here.parent_semantic_invariant: Generation proceeds through sexed bodies, an interior receptacle, gestational change, and eventual emergence.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.parent_surprising_reach: The human sequence is mirrored by a complete livestock scene of estrus, stallion display, threatened mounting, uncertain conception, and visible pregnancy.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.name: Human gestation and birth
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.scene_or_process: A female body receives and carries an interior growth in the womb until birth and postpartum emergence.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.active_motifs: female sex (quranic:root_000058:B001/m01); interior pregnancy or fruit (quranic:root_000357:B002/m01); womb as the child's growing receptacle (quranic:root_000552:B003/m01); delivery of the carried fetus (quranic:root_001657:B002/m01); birth and postpartum blood (quranic:root_001533:B005/m01)
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.synthesis: The surface statement is expanded into a role-complete bodily process: female participant, womb-container, carried growth, delivery, and postpartum outcome. The pregnancy motif also preserves its plant-fruit extension without merging the two entities.

channel_subchannels_anchored_here.parent_semantic_invariant: Generation proceeds through sexed bodies, an interior receptacle, gestational change, and eventual emergence.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.parent_surprising_reach: The human sequence is mirrored by a complete livestock scene of estrus, stallion display, threatened mounting, uncertain conception, and visible pregnancy.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.name: Livestock courtship and uncertain conception
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.scene_or_process: A female desires mating, a stallion rises and bellows before mounting, and later signs either confirm pregnancy or disclose failed conception.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.active_motifs: female animal seeking the male (quranic:root_000248:B009/m01); stallion rising over females (quranic:root_000745:B003/m01); stallion's warning bellow before attack (quranic:root_001662:B005/m01); pregnancy becoming visibly apparent in ewe or camel (quranic:root_000531:B010/m01); suspected pregnancy that fails or is lost (quranic:root_000544:B013/m01)
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.synthesis: The lexical evidence forms a distinct animal reproductive sequence rather than an undifferentiated fertility theme. Display, threat, mating readiness, and uncertain gestation make generation vulnerable to failure as well as productive completion.

channel_subchannels_anchored_here.parent_semantic_invariant: Value remains productive when goods, payment, and assigned shares circulate; blockage turns circulation into stagnation and loss.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.parent_surprising_reach: The moral economy is rendered through a literal marketplace with pricing, sale, circulation, wage, and market stagnation.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.name: Wage, assigned share, and continuing yield
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.scene_or_process: Work generates an agreed payment, provision is apportioned, and a continuing grant returns benefit to its recipient.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.active_motifs: wage or recompense for work (quranic:root_000015:B001/m01); fee fixed for a task (quranic:root_000248:B005/m01); apportioned provision (quranic:root_000560:B001/m01); worker's wage or ration (quranic:root_001046:B004/m01); continuing grant or provision (quranic:root_000240:B006/m01)
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.synthesis: Reward is a structured return on action: a task, a fixed fee, an apportioned share, and a continuing flow. The channel keeps payment distinct from botanical yield while preserving their common productive-return invariant.

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak söz öbeği, ana ekseni ayıbın ve çirkinliğin karşıtı olan güzel nitelik olarak kurar. Güzelliğin bir şeyi güzel kılması ve gerçek sayılan süsün kişiyi hiçbir durumda ayıplı kılmaması da bu ekseni destekler; ancak ilki güzelleştirme eylemiyle, ikincisi ise süs araçlarıyla karıştırılmaması gereken sınır açıklamalarıdır.
identity_judgment.boundary_note: Bu dal güzel olma niteliğini anlatır; güzelleştirme eylemi ile bezenmekte kullanılan şeyler ayrı dallarda kalır.

lexicalization_scope.note: Tanım, yalın güzel olma niteliğini temel alır; yüz ve güzelliğin bir şeyi güzel kılmasıyla ilgili kalıpları bu özün bağlama bağlı gerçekleşmeleri olarak ayırır.

facets.statement: Kavram, bezenmek için kullanılan veya kişiyi ya da şeyi bezeyen her türlü nitelik ve unsurun ortak adıdır.

Dünyalık tür, malı, eşyayı ve toplumsal saygınlığı kişiyi bezeyen dışsal unsurlar olarak bir araya getirir.

lexicalization_scope.note: Tanım genel çirkinlik ve kötülük çekirdeğini verir; kişi, iş ve sözle kurulan kalıplar bu çekirdeğin bağlama bağlı uygulamaları olarak ayrı tutulur.

concept_map.definition: Bir kişinin, varlığın, niteliğin, işin ya da durumun iyi ve güzelin karşıtı olacak biçimde çirkin, kötü veya kusurlu sayılmasıdır.

facets.statement: Temel anlam, bir şeyin çirkin, kötü veya nitelikçe bozuk oluşuna ilişkin olumsuz değerlendirmedir.
Bu değerlendirme kişiye, söze, işe, davranışa ve utanç verici bir duruma uygulanabilir.

source_synthesis.common_summary: Kaynaklar çirkinlik ve kötülüğü ortak çekirdek olarak sunar; kötü söz, kötü iş ve kötü kişi gibi kullanımlar bu çekirdeğin farklı taşıyıcılara uygulanmasıdır.

concept_gloss.applicability: Bir kişi, nitelik, iş, söz veya durum iyi ve güzelin karşıtı olarak değerlendirildiğinde dalın bütün çekirdeğini karşılar.

error_profile.preserves: Hem çirkinlik değerlendirmesini hem de nitelikçe kötülük çekirdeğini korur.

contextual_glosses.applicability: Bir kişinin, varlığın veya niteliğin doğrudan olumsuz değerlendirilmesinde doğal bir karşılıktır.

error_profile.preserves: Niteliksel kötülük ile çirkinlik değerlendirmesini birlikte korur.

contextual_glosses.applicability: Olumsuz değerlendirmenin bir davranışa, işe ya da söze uygulandığı bağlamlarda kullanılır.

error_profile.preserves: Kötülük değerlendirmesinin iş ve söz üzerindeki bağlamsal uygulamasını korur.

error_profile.collision: Birini üzme ve ona kötü davranma dalıyla karışır.

neighbor_distinctions.shared_zone: İki dal da iyinin karşıtı olan kötülük ve kötü kişi değerlendirmesinde kesişir.
neighbor_distinctions.distinction: Komşu dal kötülük alanını öne çıkarır; bu dalın çekirdeğinde kötülükle birlikte çirkinlik ve niteliksel bozukluk da bulunur.

neighbor_distinctions.neighbor_only: Birinin üzülmesi, istenmeyen bir şeye uğraması ya da kötü muamele görmesidir.

neighbor_distinctions.distinction: Bu dal bir nitelik veya değerlendirme bildirir; komşu dal ise bir kişi üzerindeki kötü etkiyi ya da ona yönelen davranışı bildirir.

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak ifadesi dalı birini üzmek, ona istemediği bir şey yaşatmak veya ona iyi davranmanın tersini yapmak çevresinde açıkça kurar.
identity_judgment.boundary_note: Salt çirkinlik değerlendirmesi bu dala girmez; bir kişide sıkıntı doğması, kötü bir şeyin ona ulaşması veya ona kötü davranılması gerekir.

lexicalization_scope.note: Genel etki çekirdeği korunur; birine kötü davranma, kötü son döngüsü ve başına kötü bir şey gelme anlamları yalnız kendi biçim ve kalıpları içinde verilir.

concept_map.definition: Bir kişiyi üzmek, ona istemediği bir durum yaşatmak ya da ona iyi davranmanın tersine kötü davranmaktır; edilgen kullanımda kişinin başına onu üzen bir şey gelmesini de anlatır.

facets.statement: Temel anlam, bir kişide sevinmenin karşıtı olan üzüntü veya sıkıntı etkisini doğurmaktır.
Eylem, birine iyi davranmanın tersine kötü davranmak veya ona kötülük etmek biçiminde genişler.

source_synthesis.common_summary: Kaynaklar birini üzme ve ona istemediği bir şey yaşatma çekirdeğinde birleşir; kötü davranma ve kötü bir sonuçla karşılaşma bu etkinin eylemsel ve edilgen görünümleridir.

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak ifadesi genel bedensel kusur ve hastalık anlamını açıkça verir, ayrıca belirli bir söz diziminde beyaz lekeli deri hastalığını örtülü biçimde belirtir.
identity_judgment.boundary_note: Genel hastalık çekirdeği ile belirli deri hastalığını anlatan kalıp ayrıdır; ahlaki kötülük veya birini üzme anlamı buraya taşınmaz.

lexicalization_scope.note: Çıplak biçim bedensel kusur veya hastalık alanını taşır; belirli deri hastalığının yokluğu yalnız kanıtta verilen söz kalıbına bağlı bir özelleşmedir.

concept_map.definition: Bedende bulunan bir kusur, bozukluk veya hastalıktır. Belirli bir kalıp içinde özellikle deride beyaz lekeler oluşturan hastalığın bulunmamasını örtülü biçimde anlatır.

facets.statement: Temel anlam bedensel kusurları, bozuklukları ve hastalıkları topluca kapsar.
Kanıtta verilen olumsuz kalıp, özellikle beyaz lekeli bir deri hastalığının bulunmadığını bildirir.

source_synthesis.common_summary: Kaynaklar genel bedensel kusur ve hastalık anlamında birleşir; belirli olumsuz kullanımda bunun beyaz lekeli deri hastalığına yönelik örtülü bir anlatım olduğunu gösterir.

concept_gloss.applicability: Genel ad olarak bedendeki kusur ve hastalıkları kapsar; belirli deri hastalığı okuması ayrıca bağlama bağlıdır.

error_profile.preserves: Genel bedensel kusur ile hastalık çekirdeğini birlikte korur.

error_profile.preserves: Kalıba bağlı hastalık türünü ve onun bulunmaması koşulunu korur.
